proofUses.reason: Direct Lévy cumulant integration and Fourier inversion; the first absolute moment of the Lévy measure is not assumed.
Use independent edge increments and the unit-Jacobian tree-coordinate transformation.
Compose regular-variation ratios with the inverse spatial scale.
The Riesz-kernel estimate H*(H*1_B)^2 <= C(H*1_B) bounds each binary-tree integral; counting labelled shapes gives the factorial.
The omitted Lévy intensity equals the rescaled killing rate; compound-Poisson coupling dominates the resolvent by the Green kernel, and local L1 convergence passes through integrable tree diagrams.
Choose one auxiliary cutoff to control added mass, then a large spatial ball to control its second moment.
Conditional Holder and arithmetic-geometric mean reduce products to one displacement; size bias and Cauchy-Schwarz separate volume and spatial moments.
Finite-volume Russo expands the cluster-union increment. Weighted two-cluster BK/tree bounds justify exhaustion and parameter integration.
The cumulant Euler identity gives one-edge replacement by two resolvent steps and a joining displacement; cutting a marked edge yields the binary-tree split recurrence.
Lexicographic induction isolates the n+1 self terms. The signed ODE limit and diagram recurrence identify the constants; collision factorization and boundary moments remain inputs.
A path-power tree bound controls all even spatial weights. BK/Harris bound the one-point derivative error by a four-point collision.
Induction in the even degree identifies all directional moments; polarization gives the polynomial one-point limits.
BK/Harris bound each split error by an (n+2)-point collision. The relative error is O(r^(3 alpha-d)); the joining-ball Riemann sum retains r^q.
The normalized Euclidean endpoint assumptions supply all scalar, displacement and factorization inputs above d=3 alpha; the diagram induction then gives the random-measure limit.

BK is applied with the nonnegative full target weight before multinomial expansion. Symmetry then cancels odd terms, retaining the exact leading coefficient two; finite-box integration proves local absolute continuity.

An induction through the upper hierarchy uses the strict gap 2+alpha>2alpha. Sharp susceptibility supplies every spatial upper moment for alpha<2 and arbitrary normalized norms; no spatial equivalent or isotropic limit is asserted.

Holder on a uniform cluster point followed by volume-biased Cauchy-Schwarz retains V^(n-1). The odd volume-moment upper bound in terms of m2/chi remains an explicit input; it is not replaced by a tree-graph bound.

The marked common-cluster error is bounded with two extra marks. At d=3alpha its relative size is O(V^2), hence negligible by the independently proved V->0. General norm-ball Riemann sums retain the joining radius power.

The one-point ODE induction has positive gap k-alpha at even k>=2. Volume equivalents and the factorized mixed derivative supply GY8M; Y3SX then gives tightness and uniqueness of the volume-biased random-measure limit. No interacting deficit limit is inferred.
The proof bounds the cutoff kernel by a strictly smaller full kernel, gets all volume moments from the tree-graph moment bound (Y84V), and bounds displacements by path length.
The proof uses finiteness from 0CUF, the first-moment deficit bound (NJF3) with E|K|^3 <= 3 chi^5 from the tree-graph bound (Y84V), and a reciprocal differential inequality.

The proof starts from 7F5O, closes the second-moment equation (6H7C, NJF3, IXEZ), and inducts using the factorization error bound (XXTP), the tree-graph bound (Y84V) and the linear induction step of 5O1G.
The proof differentiates the finite-volume projected moment (7WIO), bounds the closed-pivotal terms by finite BK (BNY8), and passes to the limit by dominated convergence.
The proof applies the multipoint tree-graph bound (AFH6) over the (2m-3)!! shapes with 2m-1 edges (SO5J) and sums the projected square along the root-to-leaf path.
The proof bounds the deficit by BK (JRCI) and Harris (X5SS), subtracts the exact identity of 57RX, and bounds the collision sums by 5OBO and the third-moment bound (Y84V).
The proof gets finite moments from the tree-graph bound (Y84V) and 0CUF, writes the equation of 57RX with the error of 6DOC, and applies the linear ODE regimes of GAF9.
